1147.text: CaO and NaCl have the same crystal structure and approximately the same ionic radii. If U is the lattice energy of NaCl , the approximate lattice energy of CaO is
1147.sol: Lattice energy =- q₁ q₂ r^2 where q₁ and q₂ are charges on ions and r is the distance between them. Since interionic distances in CaO and NaCl are similar, (larger cation has smaller anion and vice versa) therefore, r is almost the same. Therefore, lattice energy depends only on charge. Since the magnitude of charge on Na ⁺ and Cl ⁻ ions is unity and that on Ca ²⁺ and O ²⁻ ions is 2 each, therefore, the lattice energy of CaO is four times the lattice energy of NaCl , i.e., 4 U .

options: Erection will be able to occur, but ejaculation will not be possible.

71779.subject: Chemistry
71779.text: 2 MnO _ 2(s) + 2 NH ₄^+ + 2e^- Mn ₂ O _ 3(s) + 2 NH _ 3(aq) + H ₂ O _ (l) Which of the following cell exhibits above net reduction reaction?
options: H ₂ - O ₂ Feul cell
71779.sol: The given reaction is the reduction half-reaction that takes place at the cathode in a Leclanche cell (also known as a dry cell). At the cathode, manganese dioxide is reduced in the presence of ammonium ions to form manganese(III) oxide (or MnO(OH)), ammonia, and water. The overall cathode reaction is: 2 MnO _ 2(s) + 2 NH ₄^+ + 2e^- Mn ₂ O _ 3(s) + 2 NH _ 3(aq) + H ₂ O _ (l) Thus, the cell that exhibits this net reduction reaction is the Leclanche cell. Answer: Leclanche cell

72582.subject: General Ability
72582.text: Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet: __________ your transfer request is concerned, we'll be discussing it at the next meeting.
72582.sol: The phrase 'is concerned' is commonly paired with 'As far as' to introduce a topic of discussion. The complete expression 'As far as [something] is concerned' means 'regarding [something]' or 'with respect to [something]'. Substituting the other options results in grammatically incorrect sentences. Therefore, 'As far as' is the most appropriate discourse marker.

106625.sol: We can classify the elements into four blocks viz., s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block depending on the type of atomic orbitals that are being filled with electrons.

106684.subject: Chemistry
106684.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106684.text: What recommendation has the IUPAC made to avoid naming disputes for new elements?
options: The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named after famous scientists.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should not be named until their discovery is proven.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named by the first laboratory to synthesize them.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named after the laboratory where they were discovered.
106684.sol: To avoid problems, the IUPAC has made a recommendation that until a new element’s discovery is proved, and its name is officially recognised, a systematic nomenclature be derived directly from the atomic number of the element using the numerical roots for 0 and numbers 1-9.

119418.sol: Anhydrides, when hydrolyzed with water, yield carboxylic acids as the final products.

120627.subject: Chemistry
120627.text: What is the chemical linkage that connects amino acids in proteins?
120627.sol: The amino acids in proteins are connected by a chemical linkage known as the "peptide bond."

120979.subject: Chemistry
120979.text: Which of the following physiological conditions is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin E in the human body?
options: Increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness
120979.sol: According to the NCERT classification of vitamins and their deficiency diseases, the deficiency of Vitamin E leads to increased fragility of red blood cells (RBCs) and muscular weakness. Osteomalacia is caused by Vitamin D deficiency, increased blood clotting time is due to Vitamin K deficiency, and xerophthalmia is caused by Vitamin A deficiency. Answer: Increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness

121114.subject: Botany
121114.text: What term is used to describe the process of standardizing the naming of living organisms?
121114.sol: Hence, there is a need to standardise the naming of living organisms such that a particular organism is known by the same name all over the world. This process is called nomenclature . Obviously, nomenclature or naming is only possible when the organism is described correctly and we know to what organism the name is attached to. This is identification. In order to facilitate the study, number of scientists have established procedures to assign a scientific name to each known organism. This is acceptable to biologis

121279.subject: Botany
121279.text: What is the main feature that differentiates Archaebacteria from other bacteria?
options: Their ability to survive in extreme conditions
121279.sol: These bacteria are special since they live in some of the most harsh habitatssuch as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles)and marshy areas (methanogens). Archaebacteria differ from other bacteriain having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible fortheir survival in extreme conditions. Methanogens are present in the gutof several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and they areresponsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of theseanimals.

121683.subject: Botany
121683.text: What is the basis of phylogenetic classification systems ?
121683.sol: The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters such as habit, color, number and shape of leaves, etc. They were based mainly on vegetative characters or on the androecium structure (system given by Linnaeus). Such systems were artificial; they separated the closely related species since they were based on a few characteristics. Also, the artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics; this is not acceptable since we know that often the v

122427.subject: Botany
122427.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Echinoderms have an incomplete digestive system 2. Asterias have a water vascular system 3. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. 4. They are triploblastic and coelomate animals. 5. Digestive system is complete with mouth on the lower (ventral) side and anus on the upper (dorsal) side
122427.sol: These animals have an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and, hence, the name Echinodermata (Spiny bodied, Figure 4.14). All are marine with organ-system level of organisation. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. They are triploblastic and coelomate animals. Digestive system in echinoderms is complete with mouth on the lower (ventral) side and anus on the upper (dorsal) side.The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which

122552.subject: Botany
122552.text: Which of the following pairs of animal phyla exclusively exhibits the same type of body symmetry as that observed in adult echinoderms?
122552.sol: Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry. Among the given options, members of the phyla Coelenterata and Ctenophora exclusively exhibit radial symmetry. Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, and Arthropoda exhibit bilateral symmetry. Members of Porifera are mostly asymmetrical. Answer: Coelenterata and Ctenophora

122722.subject: Botany
122722.text: What distinguishes a compound leaf from a simple leaf?
options: Absence of a bud in the axil
122722.sol: A leaf is said to be simple, when its lamina is entire or when incised, the incisions do not touch the midrib. When the incisions of the lamina reach up to the midrib breaking it into a number of leaflets, the leaf is called compound . A bud is present in the axil of petiole in both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axil of leaflets of the compound leaf.

123089.subject: Botany
123089.text: A fruit developed from hypanthodium inflorescence is called :

123271.subject: Botany
123271.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Stomata regulates the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange Reason: Stomata contains chloroplasts
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
123271.sol: Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

123561.subject: Botany
123561.text: Does the chromosome number increase during the S phase?
123561.sol: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cyt

123607.subject: Botany
123607.text: What is the main characteristic of metaphase?
options: Chromosomes are held together by the centromere
Chromosomes are moved into position at the center of the cell
Chromosomes are aligned at the metaphase plate
123607.sol: At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell. Hence, the metaphase is characterised by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by i

123798.subject: Botany
123798.text: Which tissue of animals and plants exhibits meiosis?
123798.sol: Gonads (testes and ovary) in animals and sporangium in plants exhibit meiosis.

123807.subject: Botany
123807.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the structures involved in cell division. List-I List-II (A) Spindle fibres (I) Primary constriction (B) Kinetochore (II) Attachment site for spindle fibres (C) Centromere (III) Microtubular structures that move chromosomes (D) Centrosome (IV) Organelle that radiates aster rays Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123807.sol: Spindle fibres are microtubular structures that attach to chromosomes and facilitate their movement towards opposite poles. Kinetochores are small disc-shaped structures present on the surface of the centromere, which serve as the attachment sites for spindle fibres. The centromere is the primary constriction of a chromosome that holds two sister chromatids together. The centrosome is an organelle containing two centrioles that radiates out microtubular aster rays during prophase to form the mitotic apparatus. Answ

123858.subject: Botany
123858.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During the S phase of the cell cycle, the amount of DNA per cell doubles but the chromosome number remains the same. Reason (R): During DNA replication in the S phase, the newly formed sister chromatids remain attached to each other at a common centromere. In the light of the above statements, choo
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
123858.sol: Assertion (A) is a correct statement. During the synthesis phase (S phase) of the cell cycle, DNA replication takes place. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2 C , it increases to 4 C . However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had 2n chromosomes at G ₁ , it will still have 2n chromosomes after the S phase. Reason (R) is also a correct statement and provides the correct explanation for the Assertion. The chromosome number is determined by counting the number of centromeres. During

123865.subject: Botany
123865.text: Read the following statements regarding mitotic metaphase: (A) Complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of this phase. (B) Each chromosome is made up of four sister chromatids. (C) Spindle fibres attach directly to the centromeres of the chromosomes. (D) Chromosomes are moved to the spindle equator and get aligned along the metaphase plate. How many of the above statements are correct?
123865.sol: Statement (A) is correct as the complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the onset of metaphase, allowing chromosomes to spread through the cytoplasm. Statement (B) is incorrect because a mitotic metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, not four. Statement (C) is incorrect because spindle fibres attach to small disc-shaped structures called kinetochores present at the surface of the centromeres, not directly to the centromeres themselves. Statement (D) is correct as the alignment of ch

123899.subject: Botany
123899.text: A meiocyte has 24 chromosomes with a DNA content of 2C at the G₁ phase of its cell cycle. What will be the chromosome number and DNA content respectively at the stage of meiotic prophase I where chromosomes are fully condensed, and at the end of the meiotic division that resembles normal mitosis?
123899.sol: At the G₁ phase, the meiocyte has 24 chromosomes and a DNA content of 2C. During the S phase, DNA replication occurs, doubling the DNA content to 4C, but the chromosome number remains the same (24). The stage of meiotic prophase I where chromosomes are fully condensed is diakinesis. At this stage, the cell has not yet divided, so the chromosome number is still 24 and the DNA content is 4C. The meiotic division that resembles normal mitosis is Meiosis II. At the end of Meiosis II, the homologous chromosomes and sist

124185.subject: Botany
124185.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Centromere holds a single chromatid 2. Kinetochores are present on the sides of centromere 3. Chromosomes are classified into three types 4. Acrocentric chromosome has centromere located in the middle
124185.sol: Every chromosome (visible only in dividing cells) essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc shaped structures called kinetochores are present.

124237.subject: Botany
124237.text: Chromosome Types Centromere Position A. Metacentric 1. Centromere near the end, forming one very short and one long arm B. Sub-metacentric 2. Centromere in the middle, forming two equal arms C. Acrocentric 3. Centromere slightly away from the middle, forming one short and one long arm D. Telocentric 4. Centromere at the end, forming one very short arm
124237.sol: Metacentric chromosomes have centromeres in the middle.Sub-metacentric chromosomes have centromeres slightly away from the middle.Acrocentric chromosomes have centromeres near the end.Telocentric chromosomes have centromeres at the end.

124380.subject: Botany
124380.text: Glycosylation of proteins is done by
124380.sol: Proteins synthesised by rough endoplasmic reticulum and lipids synthesised by smooth endoplasmic reticulum reach the cisternae of Golgi apparatus. Here, they combine with carbohydrates to form glycoproteins and glycolipids.

124487.subject: Botany
124487.text: What type of meristems contribute to the elongation of the plants along their axis?
124487.sol: The primary meristems of the plants principally contribute to the elongation of the plants along their axis. You also know that in dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms, the lateral meristems, vascular cambium and cork-cambium appear later in life. These are the meristems that cause the increase in the girth of the organs in which they are active. This is known as secondary growth of the plant

125234.subject: Botany
125234.text: In Glycine max, the product of biological nitrogen fixation is transported from the root nodules to other parts as:
125234.sol: Along with the transpiration stream the nodules of some plants like glycine max or soyabean export the fixed nitrogen in the form of ureides. These compounds have a high nitrogen to carbon ratio.

125823.subject: Botany
125823.text: What is the primary component of the exine that makes it resistant?
125823.sol: Pollen grains are generally spherical measuring about 25-50 micrometers in diameter. It has a prominent two-layered wall. The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin which is one of the most resistant organic material known . It can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkali. No enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is so far known. Pollen grain exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent. Pollen grains are wellpreserved as fossils because of the pre

125903.subject: Botany
125903.text: What are the usual floral rewards provided to animals by flowers?
125903.sol: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar. When the flowers are small, a number of flowers are clustered into an inflorescence tomake them conspicuous. Animals are attracted to flowers by colour and/or fragrance. The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odours to attract these animals. To sustain animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals. Nectar and pollen grains are the usual floral rewards. For harvesting the reward(s) from the

125937.subject: Botany
125937.text: What is formed when the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei?
125937.sol: After entering one of the synergids, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid. One of the male gametes moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus thus completing the syngamy. This results in the formation of a diploid cell, the zygote. The other male gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei located in the central cell and fuses with them to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN ). As this involves the fusion of three haploid nuclei it is termed triple

125988.subject: Botany
125988.text: What is one major problem associated with hybrid seeds?
options: They need to be produced every year
125988.sol: Hybrid varieties of several of our food and vegetable crops are being extensively cultivated. Cultivation of hybrids has tremendously increased productivity. One of the problems of hybrids is that hybrid seeds have to be produced every year. If the seeds collected from hybrids are sown, the plants in the progeny will segregate and do not maintain hybrid characters. Production of hybrid seeds is costly and hence the cost of hybrid seeds become too expensive for the farmers. If these hybrids are made into apomicts, t

126681.subject: Botany
126681.text: Many elements are found in living organisms either free or in the form of compounds. Which of the following is not found in living organisms?
126681.sol: Silicon is not found in living organisms.

126891.subject: Botany
126891.text: Assertion: Secondary metabolites are produced in small quantities and their extraction from the plant is difficult and expensive. Reason : Secondary metabolites can be commercially produced by using tissue culture technique.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126891.sol: Secondary metabolites are biosynthetically derived from primary metabolites but more limited in distribution in plant kingdom, being restricted to a particular taxonomic group. Secondary metabolites are accumulated by plants in smaller quantities as compared to primary metabolites. Also, they are synthesised in specialised cell types at distinct developmental stages, making their extraction and purification difficult and expensive. By the culture media using tissue culture techniques, secondary metabolites can be p

127067.subject: Botany
127067.text: Assertion : The concentration of methane in the atmosphere has more than doubled in the last 250 years. Reason : Wetlands and rice fields are the major sources of methane.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
127067.sol: Hydrocarbon are major air pollutants. Methane is produced naturally during decomposition of organic matter, incomplete biomass combustion. Its concentration was 700 ppb in pre industrial times and 1750 ppb in 2000 . So the concentration has more than doubled in the last 250 years. Flooded paddy fields, marshes, cattles etc. are the major sources of this gas.

127861.subject: Botany
127861.text: Ten percent law of energy transfer in a food chain is given by
127861.sol: According to Lindeman's law of trophic efficiency, the efficiency of energy transfer from one trophic level to next is about 10 % .

127994.subject: Zoology
127994.text: What do the female reproductive organs in frogs include?
127994.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is u

128014.subject: Zoology
128014.text: Which of the following is/are true
options: Food is captured from tongue and by the action of HCl and gastric juices starts digesting in stomach
Then reaches duodenum mixes with bile and pancreatic juice
Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juice digests carbohydrate and protein
128014.sol: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. Digestion of food takes place by the action of HCl and gastric juices secreted from the walls of the stomach. Partially digested food called chyme is passed from the stomach to the first part of the intestine, the duodenum. The duodenum receives bile from gall bladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine. Digested food is abs

128336.subject: Zoology
128336.text: What is the location of adrenal glands in the human body?
128336.sol: Our body has one pair of adrenal glands, one at the anterior part of each kidney (Figure 19.4 a). The gland is composed of two types of tissues. The centrally located tissue is called the adrenal medulla, and outside this lies the adrenal cortex.Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate metabolism causing acute weakness and fatigue leading to a disease called Addison’s disease. The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine.

128486.subject: Zoology
128486.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions Reason: Secretin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128486.sol: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen

Reason: Systemic circulation consists of flow of oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to all parts of the body and deoxygenated blood from different parts to right atrium.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

If both assertion and reason are false.

129193.subject: Zoology
129193.text: What are the two types of axons?
options: Nodes of Ranvier and Schwann cells
129193.sol: Based on the number of axons and dendrites, neurons are divided into three types: multipolar (with one axon and two or more dendrites), bipolar (with one axon and one dendrite), and unipolar (cell body with one axon only).Nissl’s granules are granular bodies in the cell body of a neuron. They are composed of typical cell organelles and are also present in the dendrites. The synaptic knob is a bulb-like structure at the distal end of the axon of a neuron. It possesses synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters.

130860.subject: Zoology
130860.text: What is the function of mons pubis in the female external genitalia?
options: To partially cover the opening of the vagina
A cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair
To lie at the upper junction of the two labia minora
130860.sol: The female external genitalia include mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris . Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair . The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, which extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening. The labia minora are paired folds of tissue under the labia majora. The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called hymen. The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of t

130888.subject: Zoology
130888.text: What does the middle piece of a sperm possess?
options: The middle piece of a sperm possesses a diploid nucleus
The middle piece of a sperm possesses a haploid nucleus
The middle piece of a sperm possesses numerous mitochondria
The middle piece of a sperm possesses enzymes that help fertilization
130888.sol: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail. A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of sperm. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome. The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum. The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail that facilitate sperm motility essential for fertilisation. The human male ejaculates

130922.subject: Zoology
130922.text: What is the chromosome pattern in a human female?
130922.sol: As you know the chromosome pattern in the human female is XX and that in the male is XY. Therefore, all the haploid gametes (ova) produced by the female have the sex chromosome X whereas in the male gametes (sperms) the sex chromosome could be either X or Y, hence, 50 per cent of sperms carry the X chromosome while the other 50 per cent carry the Y. After fusion of the male and female gametes the zygote would carry either XX or XY depending on whether the sperm carrying X or Y fertilised the ovum. The zygote carryi

131339.subject: Zoology
131339.text: Both corpus luteum and macula lutea are
131339.sol: Both corpus luteum and macula lutea are characterised by a yellow colour. After an egg is released from the ovary, the cells that line the ovarian follicle change shape and colour to become a corpus luteum (yellow body). Macula lutea is the yellowish spot present at the posterior pole of eye. Lutein, zeaxanthin, -carotene and -cryptoxanthin are responsible for its yellow colouration.

131668.subject: Zoology
131668.text: Select the incorrect statement for the given figure.
options: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strands and vice-versa.
Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds.
Always a purine comes opposite to a pyrimidine. This generates non-uniform distance between the two strands of
131668.sol: The salient features of the Double-helix structure of DNA are as follows: (i) It is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside. (ii) The two chains have antiparallel polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5' → 3', the other has 3' → 5'. (iii) The bases in two strands are paired through hydrogen bonds (H-bonds) forming base pairs (bp). Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strands and vice-versa. Similarly, Gu

132491.subject: Zoology
132491.text: Which of the following organisms exhibits female heterogamety?
132491.sol: Female heterogamety is a type of sex determination where the female produces two different types of gametes. In birds (such as fowl), the sex determination is of the ZZ-ZW type, where females are heterogametic (ZW) and males are homogametic (ZZ). Drosophila and humans exhibit the XX-XY type of sex determination, which is an example of male heterogamety. Grasshoppers exhibit the XX-XO type of sex determination, which is also an example of male heterogamety. Answer: Fowl

132571.subject: Zoology
132571.text: Mating of an organism to a double recessive in order to determine whether it is hom ozygous or heterozygous for a character under consideration is called
132571.sol: Test cross is a cross made to identify hidden recessive alleles in an individual of unknown genotype. This individual is crossed with one that is homozygous for the allele being investigated (i.e., a homozygous recessive). The homozygous recessive individual may be the parent of the individual being investigated.

132612.subject: Zoology
132612.text: Which of the following cross will produce terminal flower in garden pea?
132612.sol: Axillary position (A) is dominant over terminal (a) position. When Aa Aa is crossed we get 3: 1 ratio. of axillary and terminal flowers.

132926.subject: Zoology
132926.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding evolutionary evidences. List-I List-II (A) Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins (I) Divergent evolution (Homology) in plants (B) Thorns and Tendrils of Bougainvillea and Cucurbita (II) Convergent evolution (Analogy) in aquatic vertebrates (C) Eyes of Octopus and Mammals (III) Convergent evolution (Analogy) in diverse taxa (D) Vertebrate hearts (IV) Divergent evolution (Homology) in an
132926.sol: (A) Flippers of penguins and dolphins have different anatomical origins but perform the similar function of swimming, representing convergent evolution (analogy) in aquatic vertebrates. (B) Thorns and tendrils of Bougainvillea and Cucurbita are modified axillary buds (same origin) performing different functions, representing divergent evolution (homology) in plants. (C) Eyes of octopus and mammals differ in their retinal position and structure but perform the same visual function, representing convergent evolution

133874.subject: Zoology
133874.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The Lactic acid bacteria produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins Reason: LAB improves curd's nutritional quality by increasing vitamin D
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133874.sol: During growth, the LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins. A small amount of curd added to the fresh milk as inoculum or starter contain millions of LAB, which at suitable temperatures multiply, thus converting milk to curd, which also improves its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12.

Dissociation of the RNA polymerase at the terminator
6a0e277b165ae1327797b409.sol: In bacterial transcription, the RNA polymerase holoenzyme consists of a core enzyme and a (sigma) factor. The core enzyme is responsible for the polymerization of ribonucleotides during the elongation phase. The factor is essential for the specific recognition of the promoter sequence on the DNA. It allows the RNA polymerase to bind tightly to the promoter and initiate transcription. 6a13e469688ac6d0667aad69.text: Based on T.H. Morgan's experimental observations in Drosophila , which of the following statements correctly defines the term 'linkage'?
options: The generation of non-parental gene combinations in the offspring
The physical association of two or more genes on a chromosome
The independent assortment of genes located on different chromosomes
The mapping of gene positions using crossover frequencies
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad69.sol: T.H. Morgan coined the term 'linkage' to describe the physical association of genes on a chromosome. He observed that when two genes in a dihybrid cross were situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations was much higher than the non-parental type. The generation of non-parental gene combinations is termed 'recombination'. The independent assortment of genes applies to genes located on different chromosomes, which do not show linkage. During unfavorable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips Which of the followi
95850.sol: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. The body moves along decaying twigs and leaves engulfing organic material. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls. They are extremely resistant and survive for many years, even under adverse conditions. The spores are dispersed by air currents.

306623.subject: Physics
306623.text: Suppose F_ pp , F_ pn , and F_ nn represent the magnitudes of the nuclear force exerted by a proton on a proton, a proton on a neutron, and a neutron on a neutron, respectively. For a separation distance of 1 fm ,
options: F_ pp < F_ pn = F_ nn
F_ pp = F_ pn = F_ nn
F_ pp > F_ pn > F_ nn
F_ pp > F_ pn = F_ nn
306623.sol: The strong nuclear force is a fundamental force that acts between nucleons (protons and neutrons). One of the key properties of the strong nuclear force is that it is charge-independent. This means that the nuclear force between any two nucleons does not depend on their electric charges. Therefore, for a given separation distance (such as 1 fm ), the magnitude of the nuclear force between two protons ( F_ pp ), a proton and a neutron ( F_ pn ), and two neutrons ( F_ nn ) is exactly the same. F_ pp = F_ pn = F_ nn
